value.name: rabbi officiates wedding ceremony
value.description: Rabbi Bolensky delivers a long, food-themed wedding blessing and asks Doyle and Marylin to marry each other.
evidence: RABBI The main course -- Mature Love -- a hearty stew, cooked slowly in the oven of companionship until the meat falls off the bone. And then -- dessert. The reward for years spent together -- the sweetness of a Life Well Lived. A sorbet of grandchildren, followed by the decafe demitasse of retirement.
RABBI BOLENSKY Do you Chaim David Doyle, take Marylin to be the Barbara to your Wolfgang though the lean years as well as those that are heavily marbled?
RABBI BOLENSKY And do you, Marylin Rexroth, take Chaim to be the roux in your bechamel? The stock in your sauce?
RABBI BOLENSKY Then, by the power vested in me by the state of California, and as the maitre'd in the Prix Fixe Four Star Restaurant of Life, I now pronounce you -- man and wife...

value.name: couple kisses after pronouncement
value.description: After the rabbi pronounces them married, Doyle and Marylin kiss while the crowd cheers and applauds.

value.name: reception begins on the grounds
value.description: The scene shifts to the wedding reception on the grounds, where guests mingle after the ceremony.

value.name: Miles broods at reception
value.description: Miles stands darkly brooding at the reception, signaling his discomfort or resentment.

value.name: Wrigley shows Miles Tiffany box contents
value.description: Wrigley opens a Tiffany box and shows Miles a gift, prompting a reaction.
evidence: Wrigley opens a Tiffany box to show him the contents.

value.name: Miles mocks berry spoons
value.description: Miles reacts with disdain when Wrigley reveals the gift is a set of berry spoons.
evidence: MILES Spoons! Honestly Wrigley, I'm surprised at you. What is this? Some Martha Stewart suggestion? Those are the most cockamamie things I've ever --

value.name: Wrigley questions Miles anger
value.description: Wrigley pushes back on Miles's hostility and asks why he is so angry.

value.name: Miles laments not being the club sandwich
value.description: Miles answers wistfully with a cryptic remark that suggests envy of a simpler, more desirable relationship arrangement.
evidence: Miles sounds wistful: MILES Why couldn't we be the club sandwich?
